rv.q: Her story should be remembered, both for its inspiration on an individual level and its important intersections with pivotal events in American history.
This memory play is stuffed to the gills with many incidents from the background of a woman who survived.
It is a weighty though rewarding journey from start to finish.
Such scenes make the play more than worth seeing, and the shallower bits, which are rescued by the killer cast, make it doubly–triply so.

Ilesa Duncan’s production, featuring a nimble cast of three women playing multiple roles (LaKecia Harris, Arielle Leverett, Jenise Sheppard), does an admirable job of breathing new life into the show for which Holland (who died in 2006) remains best known.

cn.t: Holland's autobiographical play delights critics with its poignant storytelling and nimble performances, balancing humor with gravity as it traces her journey from Mississippi poverty to activism and academia.
